verses.pali: “Asantasannivāsañca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi santasannivāsañca.
verses.english: “Mendicants, I will teach you about living with bad people and living with good people.

verses.pali: Taṁ suṇātha, sādhukaṁ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmī”ti.
verses.english: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

verses.pali: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṁ.
verses.english: “Yes, sir,” they replied.

verses.pali: Bhagavā etadavoca:
verses.english: The Buddha said this:

verses.pali: “Kathañca, bhikkhave, asantasannivāso hoti, kathañca asanto sannivasanti?
verses.english: “What is it like living with bad people? How do bad people live together?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, therassa bhikkhuno evaṁ hoti:
verses.english: It’s when a senior mendicant thinks:

verses.pali: ‘theropi maṁ na vadeyya, majjhimopi maṁ na vadeyya, navopi maṁ na vadeyya;
verses.english: ‘No mendicant, whether senior, middle, or junior, should admonish me;

verses.pali: therampāhaṁ na vadeyyaṁ, majjhimampāhaṁ na vadeyyaṁ, navampāhaṁ na vadeyyaṁ.
verses.english: and I shouldn’t admonish any mendicant, whether senior, middle, or junior.

verses.pali: Thero cepi maṁ vadeyya ahitānukampī maṁ vadeyya no hitānukampī, noti naṁ vadeyyaṁ viheṭheyyaṁ passampissa nappaṭikareyyaṁ.
verses.english: If a mendicant—whether senior, middle, or junior—were to admonish me, they wouldn’t be sympathetic, and I’d bother them by saying “No!” And anyway I wouldn’t deal with it even if I saw what I did wrong.’

verses.pali: Majjhimo cepi maṁ vadeyya …pe… navo cepi maṁ vadeyya, ahitānukampī maṁ vadeyya no hitānukampī, noti naṁ vadeyyaṁ viheṭheyyaṁ passampissa nappaṭikareyyaṁ’.
Majjhimassapi bhikkhuno evaṁ hoti …pe… navassapi bhikkhuno evaṁ hoti:
verses.english: And a middle or a junior mendicant also thinks:

verses.pali: ‘theropi maṁ na vadeyya, majjhimopi maṁ na vadeyya, navopi maṁ na vadeyya;
verses.english: ‘No mendicant, whether senior, middle, or junior, should admonish me;

verses.pali: therampāhaṁ na vadeyyaṁ, majjhimampāhaṁ na vadeyyaṁ, navampāhaṁ na vadeyyaṁ.
verses.english: and I shouldn’t admonish any mendicant, whether senior, middle, or junior.

verses.pali: Thero cepi maṁ vadeyya ahitānukampī maṁ vadeyya no hitānukampī noti naṁ vadeyyaṁ viheṭheyyaṁ passampissa nappaṭikareyyaṁ.
verses.english: If a mendicant—whether senior, middle, or junior—were to admonish me, they wouldn’t be sympathetic, and I’d bother them by saying “No!” And anyway I wouldn’t deal with it even if I saw what I did wrong.’

verses.pali: Majjhimo cepi maṁ vadeyya … navo cepi maṁ vadeyya ahitānukampī maṁ vadeyya no hitānukampī, noti naṁ vadeyyaṁ viheṭheyyaṁ passampissa nappaṭikareyyaṁ’.
Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, asantasannivāso hoti, evañca asanto sannivasanti.
verses.english: That’s what it’s like living with bad people; that’s how bad people live together.

verses.pali: Kathañca, bhikkhave, santasannivāso hoti, kathañca santo sannivasanti?
verses.english: What is it like living with good people? How do good people live together?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, therassa bhikkhuno evaṁ hoti:
verses.english: It’s when a senior mendicant thinks:

verses.pali: ‘theropi maṁ vadeyya, majjhimopi maṁ vadeyya, navopi maṁ vadeyya;
verses.english: ‘Any mendicant, whether senior, middle, or junior, should admonish me;

verses.pali: therampāhaṁ vadeyyaṁ, majjhimampāhaṁ vadeyyaṁ, navampāhaṁ vadeyyaṁ.
verses.english: and I should admonish any mendicant, whether senior, middle, or junior.

verses.pali: Thero cepi maṁ vadeyya hitānukampī maṁ vadeyya no ahitānukampī, sādhūti naṁ vadeyyaṁ na naṁ viheṭheyyaṁ passampissa paṭikareyyaṁ.
verses.english: If a mendicant—whether senior, middle, or junior—were to admonish me, they’d be sympathetic, so I wouldn’t bother them, but say “Thank you!” And I’d deal with it when I saw what I did wrong.’

verses.pali: Majjhimo cepi maṁ vadeyya …pe… navo cepi maṁ vadeyya hitānukampī maṁ vadeyya no ahitānukampī, sādhūti naṁ vadeyyaṁ na naṁ viheṭheyyaṁ passampissa paṭikareyyaṁ’.
Majjhimassapi bhikkhuno evaṁ hoti …pe… navassapi bhikkhuno evaṁ hoti:
verses.english: And a middle or a junior mendicant also thinks:

verses.pali: ‘theropi maṁ vadeyya, majjhimopi maṁ vadeyya, navopi maṁ vadeyya;
verses.english: ‘Any mendicant, whether senior, middle, or junior, may admonish me;

verses.pali: therampāhaṁ vadeyyaṁ, majjhimampāhaṁ vadeyyaṁ, navampāhaṁ vadeyyaṁ.
verses.english: and I’ll admonish any mendicant, whether senior, middle, or junior.

verses.pali: Thero cepi maṁ vadeyya hitānukampī maṁ vadeyya no ahitānukampī, sādhūti naṁ vadeyyaṁ na naṁ viheṭheyyaṁ passampissa paṭikareyyaṁ.
verses.english: If a mendicant—whether senior, middle, or junior—were to admonish me, they’d be sympathetic, so I wouldn’t bother them, but say “Thank you!” And I’d deal with it when I saw what I did wrong.’

verses.pali: Majjhimo cepi maṁ vadeyya …pe… navo cepi maṁ vadeyya hitānukampī maṁ vadeyya no ahitānukampī, sādhūti naṁ vadeyyaṁ na naṁ viheṭheyyaṁ passampissa paṭikareyyaṁ’.
Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, santasannivāso hoti, evañca santo sannivasantī”ti.
verses.english: That’s what it’s like living with good people; that’s how good people live together.”
